answers.answer: Shuffle the Factory cards, place a face-down number equal to players plus one on the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Place encounter tokens on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The player with the lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: Factory cards: randomly select number of players + 1; Encounter tokens: one on each of the 11 marked territories; Structure bonus: randomly choose one tile; lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

answers.answer: Put each character at its home base; put two workers, one on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining that base; place four mechs over the Faction Mat abilities, six stars by the faction emblem, six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square, four structures in their matching Player Mat boxes, four recruits on the bottom-row circles, and the remaining six workers on Produce's red rectangles. Put the action token beside the Player Mat ready for its first placement, and leave the Faction Mat one-time recruit spaces empty. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; the Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup: the piece-placement table/list and item 3, which assigns starting power and combat-card draw to the Faction Mat and starting popularity, coins and objectives to the Player Mat.

answers.answer: You may take neither action after moving your token to a different section, and you may choose either or both actions. Rusviet may repeat a section, including a Factory card; otherwise the section must differ from last turn. Top-row gains may pay a bottom-row cost. If taking both, take the top action before the bottom action; you cannot return to the top afterward. Pay every exposed red-box cost in full before the action, then choose as much or as little of the exposed green-box benefit as desired. Exact bottom-row resource costs and coin benefits depend on the Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: move to a different section; either, both, or neither actions; Rusviet repetition; top gains may pay bottom costs; full exposed red-box costs before optional green-box benefits.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and all its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. You may pay an action's resource cost using resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: an enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources; enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; pay from any territories you currently control.

answers.answer: No. A normal Move selects up to two different units and moves each one adjacent territory; the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A worker carried by a mech may later move itself, or it may move onto a mech and be carried by that mech's subsequent move. All units can pick up, carry and drop off any number of resources; only mechs may also carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: move up to two different units, one adjacent territory each; carried workers may subsequently move themselves; all units carry resources, while only mechs carry your workers and never your character.

answers.answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn. The enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leave resources behind, and you lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; having zero popularity does not prevent the retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter that territory while enemy workers control it.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers only—your workers cannot enter independently; your character/mech may enter but stops; enemy workers retreat, leave resources, and cause one popularity loss per worker, with insufficient popularity not preventing retreat. Stops override Speed.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order when there are multiple combats. Your workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order. Workers cannot independently move into or out of enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives a choice of two power or one combat card before upgrades. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discards are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives a choice of any two resources (same or different) or one popularity, before upgrades. Put traded resources on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; you cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home.
answers.evidence: Bolster: pay $1, gain two power OR one combat card; empty deck recycling rule. Trade: pay $1, gain two resources OR one popularity; traded resources require a controlled territory with a worker.

answers.answer: First pay every exposed Produce cost in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid for the current action.
answers.evidence: Produce: pay every exposed cost in full before production; choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker produces one matching token; workers come from Player Mat left to right; production may be declined; new costs affect future actions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in the exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost. Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in the exposed Deploy cost boxes; put a chosen mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake, and its uncovered ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. The exact exposed oil and metal amounts vary by mat and upgrades. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures or recruits, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade—oil equal to exposed cost boxes and cube to empty bracketed red box; Deploy—metal equal to exposed cost boxes and mech on controlled territory with your worker, never lake; completed actions may still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Build on a controlled territory containing your worker; only one structure total may occupy a territory, including opponents' structures, and lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A Mill provides its bonus production territory only while you control it; an enemy worker alone controls the territory, so the Mill cannot produce in that case. A Mine remains your personal tunnel for your unit movement even when its territory is enemy-controlled; opponents cannot use its ability.
answers.evidence: Build: controlled territory with your worker; one structure total per territory; lakes/home bases forbidden; structures cannot move or be destroyed. Control section says uncontrolled Mill cannot produce; Mine is a personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled.

answers.answer: Put the recruit permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat and immediately gain the chosen bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. Its ongoing bonus is determined by the Player Mat circle uncovered where you removed the recruit. Ongoing bonuses trigger when you or an immediate left or right neighbor takes the corresponding bottom-row action; resolve the active player first, then left, then right, stopping if a sixth star ends the game. In a two-player game the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice. The ongoing types are Upgrade: one power; Deploy: one coin; Build: one popularity; Enlist: one combat card.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit goes on any open one-time Faction Mat bonus; four two-token choices; ongoing bonus is the circle where recruit was removed. Ongoing recruits: active, left, right order and two-player opponent triggers once.

answers.answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from zero through the smaller of seven and their current power. Each may add up to one combat card per participating character or mech, including with zero dial power; Rusviet People's Army adds one additional card total if workers are present, while workers alone never fight. If both combatants have combat mech abilities, the attacker uses theirs first and then the defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; the attacker wins ties. Each player deducts their chosen dial power from the Power Track and discards every played combat card face-up; card values do not cost additional track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–4: secret simultaneous dial selection up to min(seven,current power); card limit and Rusviet exception; attacker ability first; attacker wins ties; dial power deducted and cards discarded.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources. The loser's characters, mechs and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible units and carried workers to retreat to an adjacent lake instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none, and Polania Camaraderie has the stated exception for winning an aggressor combat. A non-Saxony winner places a combat star if they have zero or one combat stars and none if they already have two; Saxony places one after each victory while it has star tokens available. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed any power through dial or cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 5–6: winner controls; losing units retreat and leave resources; attacker popularity loss and Polania exception; combat-star limits; loser draws a card only if they revealed at least one power on dial or through cards.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; discard the token and draw a card. If the character loses a contested entry, it retreats and the token stays. Put all resources, workers, mechs and structures gained on the encounter territory. Pay the encounter's printed cost, but no additional normal action cost applies and no additional mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses are gained.
answers.evidence: Encounters: after whole Move and all combats, if character remains, discard token and draw; lost contested entry leaves token; gains go to encounter territory; pay printed cost but no normal action costs or mat/recruit benefits.

answers.answer: Every player's character, on that player's first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at the available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. Each player may have at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. Use the card as a fifth action section with optional top then bottom under the normal section rule, including Rusviet's repeat exception. Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory bottom action moves one unit up to two territories in that Move action, or a character/mech with Speed up to three; Mine access and normal movement and stop restrictions apply.
answers.evidence: Factory: every player's character chooses a card on first finish of a Move action there after combat; one permanent card; fifth action section; no corresponding mat or recruit bonuses; bottom action moves one unit two spaces or three with Speed.

answers.answer: Reveal a completed objective only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, and meet all requirements at the moment you reveal it. Place a star on the objective space of the Triumph Track and return the completed card to the bottom of the objective deck; normally return your other objective card there too. Saxony may complete both starting objectives, may keep the other card after the first completed objective, and may earn up to two objective stars.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: own turn before/after action; meet all requirements at reveal; place objective Triumph Track star; return completed and normally other card; Saxony keeps the other after first and may complete both.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victories (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except for the two combat stars and Saxony's exception: Saxony has no usual limit on combat or objective stars, within its six available stars. Other players' stars do not block a goal. A placed star is permanent even if power or popularity later falls. The sixth star immediately ends the game, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: listed achievements, award-once exceptions, other players do not block, stars are permanent, sixth star ends play immediately.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect the primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning initiating units to their territories of origin; do not resolve another combat. For a neighbor's power/popularity recruit star, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor second and right neighbor third, checking for a sixth star at each step; if an earlier player placed the sixth star, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.
answers.evidence: Sixth star sequencing: bottom action benefit, coins and own recruit benefit before star; unresolved battle movement undone; active then left then right order, stopping after sixth star.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, each star is worth $4, so five stars add $20. Four normal territories plus the Factory count as seven territory counts (four plus three), worth $3 each or $21. Thirteen resources make six complete pairs; at $2 per pair, they add $12, with one resource left over. These categories add $53 to held coins, before any selected structure bonus. Your structures remain eligible for the selected structure bonus even if opponents control their territories. Ties break by workers plus mechs plus structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table at popularity 7–12: $4 per star, $3 per territory count, $2 per resource pair; Factory counts as three; odd resource ignored; structures earn bonus even if enemies control their territories; listed tie-breakers.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move back into any home base; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: a home base is not a territory; default entry prohibition with setup, forced-retreat and Crimea Wayfare exceptions; unmatched expansion bases are inactive.

answers.answer: Mountain produces metal; tundra oil; farm food; forest wood; and village workers. Lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; Control, resources and home bases: only wood, food, metal and oil are resources; resource tokens have no supply limit.

answers.answer: Yes. All units can pick up, carry and drop off any number of resources during movement, and a mech can pick up or drop resources and workers mid-movement. Mechs may carry any number of your workers but never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character or mech, not workers; a tunnel jump still costs one step, with the extra step usable before or after it. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move: all units carry resources; only mechs carry workers, never your character; Speed adds one territory to character/mechs, tunnel jump costs one step, and stops override Speed.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory occupied only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit type.
answers.evidence: Move: Enemy structure only—any unit may enter, taking control without combat; all printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.

answers.answer: You may not pay a partial cost. If you cannot afford any action, take a dead turn: move your token to a different section and take neither action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: if unable to afford any action, take a dead turn by moving the token to a different section and taking neither action; never pay only part of a cost.

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These are bonuses on the matching actions. Opponents cannot use your buildings' abilities, and enemy occupants do not take the abilities away from you; you keep them even without control. The Mill is the exception to continued use: it cannot produce when its territory is uncontrolled.
answers.evidence: Bolster/Trade: Monument adds one popularity on Bolster and Armory adds one power on Trade. Control and Build sections: you keep structure abilities without control; opponents cannot use them; uncontrolled Mill cannot produce.

answers.answer: Riverwalk is an unlockable mech ability for every faction, including Nordic, and applies to your character and all mechs, not workers. Nordic and Saxony Riverwalk across rivers to forests and mountains; Rusviet to farms and villages; Crimea to farms and tundra; Polania to villages and mountains. Nordic Swim is a separate starting ability for workers alone to cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not give Nordic mechs that ability.
answers.evidence: Riverwalk destinations table and text: character/all mechs, not workers; Nordic Swim: workers alone cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; separate abilities.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including your Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use either shortcut.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass—controlled mountains and all tunnels; Township—controlled villages and Factory; each is for character/mech Move actions.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery applies before combat and lets you pay one power to reduce the opponent's power by two, also once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Disarm and Nordic Artillery descriptions under other unlocked mech abilities.

answers.answer: With two mechs and three workers present, Rusviet People's Army allows three combat cards total (the usual one per participating character/mech plus one additional card total because workers are present). Workers alone never fight; a character or mech is still required.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army: with at least one worker, play one additional combat card total, still requiring a character/mech; two mechs and three workers allow three cards; workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets your character and mechs move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base, regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They cannot enter an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare: move from territory or home base to own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance; not an active opponent's base.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout, before combat, steals one random combat card from the opponent into your hand, once per combat and not once per unit. Crimea Coercion lets you spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of the card's value.
answers.evidence: Scout: before combat steal one random opponent combat card into your hand, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion: once per turn spend one combat card as any one resource, regardless of card value.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets characters and mechs move to and from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers with them. Polania Submerge lets characters and mechs move to and from lakes and from any lake to any other lake; it gives no special adjacent-lake retreat exception. When leaving a lake, workers there require a mech to move off, and a departing carrier cannot leave carried workers or resources behind on the lake.
answers.evidence: Seaworthy and Submerge descriptions; lake rule: workers on lakes require a mech to move off and you cannot leave carried workers or resources behind when carrier leaves.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not prevent the popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Camaraderie: no popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn; does not protect against loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; it can choose the second option after the first, and the first gain can pay the second option's cost. Pay each selected option's printed cost, and you may take as little of its benefit as desired. Unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected. The encounter card is shown to all players, its artwork shown, and its capitalized thematic text read aloud; reading every option aloud is not required. Gains go to the encounter territory.
answers.evidence: Polania Meander: up to two different options in either order; first gain can pay second cost. Encounter rules: printed costs, partial benefits, unaffordable coin/popularity options, show/read instructions, gains to encounter territory.

answers.answer: No. A character stops on entering an encounter territory and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. Resolve the encounter only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there; it does not occur before all combats finish.
answers.evidence: Encounters: character stops and cannot move again; after whole Move and all combats resolve if character remains; same rules apply during Factory Move.

answers.answer: Coins are not hidden information, though you need not reveal their total value when asked. Combat-card hand count is public, but during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal; card contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective.
answers.evidence: Public and hidden information table: coin totals need not be revealed; combat hand count public with combat concealment exception and card contents secret until revealed; objectives secret until completed and revealed.

answers.answer: Coins are the only tangible items players may exchange; in tournament play even coin exchanges for deals or alliances are forbidden. Informal agreements are unenforceable. A payment or negotiation cannot cancel combat after it is initiated by moving units onto opposing units; fight after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: coins are only tangible exchangeable items; tournament prohibition; agreements unenforceable; combat cannot be canceled after units move onto opposing units; bribes may influence outcome.

answers.answer: At popularity 0–6, score $3 per star, $2 per territory count, and $1 per complete pair of controlled resources. At 7–12, score $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per resource pair. At 13–18, score $5 per star, $4 per territory count, and $3 per resource pair. Controlled lakes count as territories; home bases do not. Score only complete resource pairs, so a leftover single resource scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Final fortune popularity table; controlled lakes count and home bases do not; resource income uses complete pairs, rounded down.

answers.answer: For each adjacency tile, count each feature only once across all your structures, and rivers do not break adjacency. Adjacent-tunnel bonus counts unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2; 2–3 pays $4; 4–5 pays $6; 6 pays $9. Adjacent-encounter bonus counts unique printed encounter locations even if their tokens have been removed: 1 pays $2; 2–3 pays $4; 4–5 pays $6; 6–7 pays $9. Adjacent-lake bonus counts unique lakes: 1 pays $2; 2–3 pays $4; 4–5 pays $6; 6–7 pays $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table: tunnels adjacent (unique printed tunnels, not Mines); encounters adjacent (unique printed encounter locations even if token removed); lakes adjacent (unique lakes) with payouts. Adjacency features count once; rivers do not break adjacency.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2; 2 pays $4; 3–4 pays $6. Structures in a row scores only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line. It pays $2 for 1, $4 for 2, $6 for 3, or $9 for 4 structures. Structures on farms and tundras are combined for scoring; 1 pays $2; 2 pays $4; 3 pays $6; 4 pays $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table: structures on tunnels, structures in a row, and structures on farms/tundras; row is longest continuous straight line and rivers do not break it.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity for each enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake. A winning defender loses none.
answers.evidence: Combat rule: winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, even workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; winning defender loses none.
